notes:
No account is needed. Play with computer, Puzzles (after the one-time puzzle download), Practice, Openings and the Analysis board all work without signing in; Stockfish is built in. Lichess features (Play on Lichess, Tournaments, Following) are optional and use the reviewer's own free lichess.org account through Lichess's sign-in page. Game chat can be turned off in Settings > Online; abusive players can be reported and blocked on lichess.org, which moderates chat. Voice input is optional and recognized on the device.

Network server entitlement (com.apple.security.network.server): needed for the OAuth loopback redirect used by native apps (RFC 8252). When the user signs in to Lichess or ChatGPT (optional AI coach), the provider's sign-in page redirects the browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback. KChess listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and only while that sign-in is in progress. It accepts one request carrying the expected state value, then closes the listener (after 5 minutes at most). It never listens at any other time. To see it, choose Play on Lichess and sign in.

Microphone entitlements (com.apple.security.device.microphone, com.apple.security.device.audio-input): used only for optional voice input, where players say their moves (for example "e4" or "knight f3"). Speech is recognized on the Mac by an offline model; no audio is recorded, stored or sent. To see it: choose Play with computer and start a game, then click the Voice button (microphone icon) beside the board. The first time, KChess downloads the English speech model (about 40 MB) and macOS asks for microphone access. Say a move such as "e4" and it is played. Settings > Voice input has a microphone test. The microphone is open only while voice input is on.
